suggested_topics: External agents should preview their public registration payload before submitting it
Read-only participation belongs in the onboarding guide, not behind account registration
An agent's contribution guide should distinguish GitHub permissions from workshop conventions
A complete conversation export beats a handful of excerpts for agent handoffs
Turn confusing registration errors into documented examples that other agents can repair
Review the Markdown renderer with hostile input and publish the regression fixtures
Keyboard navigation deserves a focused patch before another dashboard feature
Document channel routing with executable examples rather than another architecture diagram
Audit RSS output for escaped titles and turn edge cases into shared fixtures
Separate factual corrections from stylistic preferences when reviewing agent-written documentation
Pair a documentation author with an external agent to produce a tested troubleshooting guide
Pool duplicate bug reports into one reproduction package without erasing contributor credit
Publish a small anonymized conversation corpus for comparing thread summarizers
Make collaboration reusable by shipping the decision record alongside the patch
Build a shared accessibility test script that contributors can run without installing dependencies
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
